summary: Phase 149O.20L.7L.1 -- HMIC-001 v1.4 Consumer-Status and Dependency-Header Repair. 149O.20L.7L independently verified the 28->30 frozen source-scope expansion is technically correct but withheld VERIFIED because HMIC-001 v1.4 itself falsely stated (HMIC-REQ-052 limb (c)'s closing paragraph, section 55.4's citation, section 55.15's verdict, and attack row 39 clause (a)) that no readiness/certification/activation code path consumes verify_class_b_deployment_conformance, when Phase 149O.20L.3 had already wired it into hatp_mandatory_cutover.py's mandatory activation-readiness assessment as the eighth readiness term -- ancestral to 149O.20L.7K's own phase entry. Independently reconstructed the exact production evidence, not from 7L's prose: import at line 74, call at line 952 inside _assess_hatp_mandatory_activation_readiness_at_root, eighth of eight readiness checks assembled, re-invoked lock-held immediately before any real HATP_MANDATORY activation write via _activate_hatp_mandatory_at_root's readiness_check callback; no other src/pcae module calls the readiness-assessment function. Independently reconstructed the exact chronology via git log --oneline main position ordering: 149O.20L.3's wiring commit e2ccb7a3 landed after 149O.20K (v1.3, contract section 53) but before 149O.20L.7K (v1.4, contract section 55) -- so section 53.4's identical zero-consumer claim was accurate when 149O.20K wrote it and is left unmodified as a legitimate historical snapshot, while section 55's language was never accurate at the moment 149O.20L.7K wrote it, not merely stale afterward. Distinguished consumption categories precisely: readiness yes (direct call), activation yes (indirect via the same lock-held readiness re-check), certification no (the HMIC validator neither calls nor is called by the verifier). Repaired narrowly, same version (HMIC-001 remains v1.4): HMIC-REQ-052 limb (c)'s closing paragraph now states the first anchor is not anticipatory while explicitly preserving the third anchor's own non-reachability rationale unweakened; a scope-clarifying note was appended to section 55.4 (its own producer-only finding was never false, only misleadingly cited by section 55.15); section 55.15's verdict sentence was corrected with an inline explanation; attack row 39 clause (a) was regrounded in the true, load-bearing non-reachability fact rather than the false zero-consumer claim, preserving legs (b)/(c) and the row's overall not-functionally-load-bearing conclusion; attack row 38's twin stale claim was also repaired (F-7L-5, narrowly, because it directly duplicates the F-7L-1 claim in the same table -- rows 33/34/36/37 were adjudicated and deferred as non-blocking, tied to a different subsystem's realignment history requiring wider reconstruction outside this phase's own evidence chain). The Depends on header was corrected from HBDC-001 v1.0 to v1.1 (F-7L-2, non-blocking, identical defect class to B-149O.20L.1-1/section 54, repaired the same way); derive_contract_versions independently confirmed to already correctly return HBDC-001=1.1 from live headers, so the mechanism itself was never stale. Added a new section 56 (Contract Repair History -- Phase 149O.20L.7L.1) documenting the repair in the section 52/section 54 precedent shape, plus a header-block Repaired-by line and Status-line update. F-7L-7 adjudicated: the two 7I/7J textual guard-test exemptions of hatp_mandatory_certification.py were tightened from whole-file to exact-occurrence granularity (a matching line's first token being import/from now still fails the test; the file's three known non-import literal occurrences continue to pass); 149O.20L.7L's own strictly stronger, unconditional AST-level guard and its frozen-path-data companion test are untouched. Verified no normative/production change: HMIC version unchanged at 1.4; HMIC-REQ-050's thirty-file enumeration byte-identical; hatp_mandatory_certification.py's own assert len(...) == 30 line unedited; producer, admin script, HBDC-001 document, and hatp_mandatory_cutover.py all byte-identical by git hash-object before/after; implementation_scope_digest independently recomputed unchanged at 65ff8ab06b5cd7feb2505742cfbb112ffd386c5b2cf34c2d7f3446d92afe15b8 (HMIC-001 is not itself a member of its own frozen set, so the contract-document edit does not enter this digest); derive_contract_versions post-repair returns HBDC-001=1.1, now agreeing exactly with the repaired header. Added a new, independent focused-regression test module (20 tests, all passing): dependency-header consistency, F-7L-1 consumer-status regression guards, a direct production-consumer guard avoiding line-number pinning, a third-anchor regression guard, attack-row coherence, and version/membership/production-immutability guards including literal pre-repair git-blob-hash pins and a pinned digest value. A/B regression classification against a disposable git worktree at this phase's true entry commit (95cfd008) over a 22-file targeted selection (HMIC/HBDC contract tests, 7K/7L/7I/7J suites, certification/cutover focused tests): 114 pre-repair failures/9 errors vs 119 post-repair failures/9 errors before test updates; node-ID diff showed exactly 6 new failures, four of which were exactly the self-pin tests this phase's own repair was expected to break (7L's own two findings-still-present pins, both explicitly carrying update-once-repaired docstrings; one 149O.20K-era row-38 wording pin; one 149O.20L.1A-era pin that was falsely comparing against live text instead of its own phase's diff window) -- all four updated and reverified passing; the remaining two are git-status-porcelain working-tree-cleanliness pins that resolve automatically once this phase's changes are committed. One pre-existing failure resolved as a side effect (a header/live-value mismatch guard that now passes because the mismatch it detected is fixed). Zero unexplained, zero security/authority/behavioral regressions. FINAL VERDICT: CONTRACT REPAIR IMPLEMENTED -- INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION PENDING. F-7L-1 and F-7L-2 repaired narrowly with no membership/production semantic change. 7J section 31 remains REPAIRED AT THE CONTRACT-AND-PRODUCTION LAYER -- INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION PENDING -- NOT CLOSED, unchanged by this phase; only 149O.20L.7L.2 may close it. All carried-forward findings (HMIC-REQ-103, 7J section 17, the permissive timestamp parser, HMIC-REQ-063) remain untouched. No Dell access, no RepositoryIdentity, no DeploymentBinding, no first-use election, no certification, no redeployment. Runtime remains Observed / observe / unavailable. HATP production remains NOT READY.
